surfaces.part: cliff face with ramp cut (vertical rock face with V-shaped strata and dark side edges)
ramp / ground surface in front of the cliff (flat speckled plane seen from above)

answer.evidence: The silhouette is a full 48px-wide tile for all 32 rows. Rows 0-15 are the vertical south cliff face: a V-shaped strata pattern, dark outline edges on the left and right, and a dark base line at row 15 where the face meets the ground. Rows 16-31 are a uniform, lightly speckled horizontal ramp surface seen from above. The column scan at x=24 shows a dark band at rows 11-13, then a uniform body from row 14 to 31. That gives a 16-row ground or ramp plane below a 16-row front face. The ramp slope itself is only implied by the flat plane, since no tread edges are drawn.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate's visible tones per tile (7) match the paving reference, and its dark edges are partly tinted (33% neutral), so it is not a pure sticker outline. The problem is the flat fill: 41% near-flat coverage against 0% in both references. The lower half of the ramp is a large, nearly uniform beige slab with no grain, speckle or per-stone shading. Only the upper chevron/diagonal strip carries texture, and it reads as about 4 lightness steps against the references' 5-6. The ramp is also noticeably flatter and less detailed than the grass and paving tiles, which have texture dots across the whole surface. A careful artist would not accept it next to the references.
